types.name: Fenrir::AmbientOcclusion
types.doc: A view's ambient occlusion (ADR-0049): ground-truth ambient occlusion (GTAO, after Intel's XeGTAO) from its depth prepass, darkening the sky's light where nearby geometry hides the sky from a surface, as in creases, corners and under objects resting on the ground. It darkens the sky's diffuse light, and its specular light by a specular occlusion made from it, never the directional, point, spot or rect lights. Transparent items take none.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether the view has it: off by default, and off costs nothing.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far round a surface other surfaces occlude it, in world units (in the camera's own, if its entity is scaled): 0.5 by default. 0 or less turns it off.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: How dark the occlusion is: 1 by default, 0 none (and no cost), and above 1 darker. It raises the occlusion to a power, so an unoccluded surface stays unoccluded however strong it is.

types.name: Fenrir::Colour
types.doc: A colour as linear red, green, blue and alpha, each a float, usually in [0, 1] (ADR-0025). Debug draw, materials and lights take it, and the renderer packs it for vertices. Colours written as sRGB hex values, as colour pickers and art tools give them, are converted when made (FromSrgb). Default constructed, it is opaque white.

types.name: Fenrir::AnamorphicStreaks
types.doc: A view's anamorphic streaks (ADR-0059): bright pixels drawn out into long, thin horizontal lines, as an anamorphic lens draws them, mixed in before the tonemap after bloom. Like bloom there is no threshold: everything streaks by the same share, and only what is bright shows it. The streaks keep the scene's energy and the tint is taken at unit luminance, so they move light, never add it. Off by default; a view with bloom off still streaks.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: The share of the streaks the view's colour is mixed with, from 0 to 1. 0 by default, which turns them off and costs nothing; a few hundredths draw long lines from lights and leave dim surfaces alone.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: How long the streaks are, from 0 (the shortest only, a few pixels either side) to 1 (the longest only, reaching most of the way across the view). 0.75 by default.

fields.name: tint
fields.doc: The streaks' colour, linear, scaled to unit luminance: its hue and saturation count, its brightness is ignored. White by default.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Image>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip`, `BoneMask` or `InstanceList`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::InstanceList>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip`, `BoneMask` or `InstanceList`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Material>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip`, `BoneMask` or `InstanceList`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Mesh>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip`, `BoneMask` or `InstanceList`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::BackgroundType
types.doc: Which kind of background a CameraBackground holds.

types.name: Fenrir::Bloom
types.doc: A view's bloom (ADR-0049): the scene blurred over ever wider areas and mixed back in before the tonemap, so bright pixels bleed light into their surroundings. There is no threshold: everything blooms by the same share, and only what is bright shows it. The blur keeps the scene's energy, so bloom moves light, never adds it.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: The share of the blur the view's colour is mixed with, from 0 to 1: 0.04 by default, a soft glow round what is several times brighter than its surroundings. 0 turns bloom off and costs nothing.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: How far the glow spreads, from 0 (the narrowest blur only, a few pixels) to 1 (the widest only, made at a sixty-fourth of the view's size). 0.7 by default.

types.name: Fenrir::ColourBackground
types.doc: A camera background of one colour, overriding the scene's.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. Black by default (Colour::Black).

types.name: Fenrir::SceneBackground
types.doc: A camera background that is the scene's own: its Sky.

types.name: Fenrir::CameraBackground
types.doc: What a camera's view shows where nothing was drawn: exactly one of SceneBackground and ColourBackground, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape. Assign a kind to change it (`camera.background = ColourBackground{Colour::Blue}`); read it through the checked view. Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::CameraDebugView
types.doc: What a view shows instead of its lit colour, to look at one of its inputs.

values.name: None
values.doc: The lit scene, tonemapped: the default.

values.name: AmbientOcclusion
values.doc: Its ambient occlusion as grey, white unoccluded, with no exposure or tonemap; black where the camera's ambient occlusion is off.

values.name: ShadowCascades
values.doc: Its lit colour, each pixel tinted by the sun's shadow cascade it reads (ADR-0050): red, green, blue and yellow from the nearest, untinted past the last or without shadows.

values.name: ShadowAtlas
values.doc: The sun's shadow atlas for this view as grey, its cascades side by side from the nearest, white nearest the sun, with no exposure or tonemap; black where nothing casts.

values.name: SpotShadowAtlas
values.doc: The frame's spot shadow atlas as grey (ADR-0050), each shadowed spot light's tile along the rows from the top left, nearest the view first, white nearest its light, with no exposure or tonemap; black where no spot light casts.

values.name: LightClusters
values.doc: Each lit pixel as the heat of how many lights it loops over (ADR-0049), its cluster's or, unclustered, every light: black for none, then blue at 1, cyan at 4, green at 16, yellow at 64 and red at 256, the most a cluster lists, on a log scale, exposed and tonemapped.

values.name: Reflections
values.doc: Its screen-space reflections (ADR-0056): at each pixel, the colour its mirror ray hit, from last frame, times how sure the hit is, exposed, vignetted, graded, tonemapped and grained; black where nothing is reflected or the camera's reflections are off. It is what a mirror there would blend, sharp: a material's roughness blurs and fades it.

values.name: ReflectionConfidence
values.doc: How sure each pixel's reflection hit is, as grey from black (no hit) to white, with no exposure or tonemap; black where the camera's reflections are off.

types.name: Fenrir::ChromaticAberration
types.doc: A view's chromatic aberration (ADR-0059): each colour channel read from its own point as the Output pass reads the scene, red moved outwards and blue inwards, more the further from the centre, as a lens bends each wavelength by its own amount. Edges near the view's corners fringe red outside and blue inside; the centre is as it is. Off by default, and off costs nothing.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: How far red and blue move apart at the view's corners, as a fraction of the distance from its centre to a corner: 0 by default, off. A few thousandths fringe the edges; a few hundredths split them.

types.name: Fenrir::ColourGrading
types.doc: A view's colour grade (ADR-0059): the look of the picture, set on the exposed scene colour before the tonemapper, in linear Rec. 709. So contrast and saturation act on scene values, mid grey stays put and the tonemapper still rolls off whatever the grade brightens, so a strong grade does not clip. Its steps run in this order: white balance, contrast, split toning, saturation, then the ASC CDL. Identity by default, and identity costs nothing.

fields.name: temperature
fields.doc: The colour temperature, in kelvin, of the light the view takes as white: 6500 by default (D65, no change). A surface lit by daylight of this temperature comes out grey, so lower cools the picture and higher warms it. Held to 2500 to 25000.

fields.name: tint
fields.doc: How far off daylight that white lies, from -1 to 1: 0 by default. Positive names a greener light, so the picture moves to magenta; negative names a magenta one, so it moves to green.

fields.name: contrast
fields.doc: The slope of the picture in stops around mid grey (0.18), which it keeps: 1 by default, above 1 more contrast, below 1 flatter, 0 all mid grey.

fields.name: shadowTint
fields.doc: The tint the shadows take, linear: white by default, and any grey is none. Only its hue and saturation count (it is scaled to unit luminance, so a grey keeps its brightness); the more saturated, the stronger.

fields.name: highlightTint
fields.doc: The tint the highlights take, as the shadows' does.

fields.name: balance
fields.doc: Where the shadows end and the highlights start, from -1 to 1: 0 by default, the split at mid grey. Positive moves it down by up to four stops, giving the highlights' tint more of the picture; negative up.

fields.name: saturation
fields.doc: How far each colour is from grey of its luminance: 1 by default, 0 grey, above 1 more saturated. After split toning, so lowering it fades the tints too.

fields.name: slope
fields.doc: The ASC CDL, the final trim, per channel: each is multiplied by its slope, then its offset is added, then negatives are clamped and the result raised to its power. The slope, 1 in each channel by default.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: The CDL's offset, added after the slope: 0 in each channel by default.

fields.name: power
fields.doc: The CDL's power, held at or above 0.001: 1 in each channel by default.

types.name: Fenrir::FilmGrain
types.doc: A view's film grain (ADR-0059): noise added after the tonemap, in the range the viewer sees, so its strength holds at any exposure. It shows most in the mid-tones and least in deep shadow and bright highlight, as film grain does, and it changes every frame. Off by default, and off costs nothing.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: How far the grain moves a pixel's brightness, at most, as a fraction of the display's range: 0 by default, off. A few hundredths are fine grain.

fields.name: response
fields.doc: How much the grain is kept to the mid-tones, from 0 to 1: 0.8 by default. 0 grains every brightness alike; 1 leaves black and white untouched.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: The side of each grain, in pixels, at least 1: 1 by default.

types.name: Fenrir::LensFlare
types.doc:
A view's lens flare (ADR-0059), after John Chapman's pseudo lens flare: ghosts of the bright parts of the view, mirrored through its centre along the line from them, and a halo ring, each colour fringed apart, mixed in before the tonemap after the streaks. Like bloom there is no threshold: the flare is the view's own light read from elsewhere, so it moves light and never adds it, and a bright sky ghosts as a faint veiling glare as a real lens does. Off by default.

A lens dirt image scales how much of the bloom and the flare each pixel takes where the lens is dirty, so a bright light lights up the smudges on it.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: The share of the flare the view's colour is mixed with, from 0 to 1. 0 by default, which turns it off and costs nothing; a few hundredths throw faint ghosts from lights.

fields.name: ghostCount
fields.doc: How many ghosts each bright point throws, from 0 to 8: 4 by default.

fields.name: ghostSpacing
fields.doc: How far apart the ghosts are along the line through the view's centre, as a share of the way from each pixel to the centre: 0.4 by default. Each ghost is read that much further along the line than the last, so ghosts past the centre land on the far side of it.

fields.name: haloRadius
fields.doc: The halo ring's radius, as a distance from the view's centre: 0 at the centre, 1 at the corners. 0.6 by default. The ring shows what is bright near the centre.

fields.name: haloWidth
fields.doc: How far the halo reaches either side of its radius, in the same distance: 0.1 by default; 0 none.

fields.name: chromaticOffset
fields.doc: How far red and blue are read apart in each ghost and the halo, along the line through the view's centre, in the same distance: 0.01 by default, so the ghosts fringe.

fields.name: dirt
fields.doc: A greyscale image of the dirt on the lens, stretched over the view; none by default. A flat image with pixels; anything else (a cubemap, a render target) has no dirt, logged once.

fields.name: dirtIntensity
fields.doc: How much more of the bloom and the flare a pixel takes where the dirt is white: its share is multiplied by 1 + dirtIntensity times the dirt's brightness, held at or below 1, so the mix stays a blend. 1 by default; 0 is no dirt. It needs no flare: dirt with the flare off scales the bloom alone.

types.name: Fenrir::Orthographic
types.doc: An orthographic projection with reversed-Z depth (ADR-0026): the near plane maps to depth 1 and the far plane to 0. The width comes from the height and the viewport's pixel size.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: The full height of what the view shows, in world units.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: The distance to the near plane along the camera's -Z, in world units.

fields.name: far
fields.doc: The distance to the far plane along the camera's -Z, in world units.

types.name: Fenrir::Perspective
types.doc: A perspective projection with an infinite far plane and reversed-Z depth (ADR-0026): the near plane maps to depth 1 and the distance to 0. The aspect comes from the viewport's pixel size.

fields.name: verticalFov
fields.doc: The vertical field of view in radians; 60 degrees by default.

fields.name: near
fields.doc: The distance to the near plane, in world units.

types.name: Fenrir::ProjectionType
types.doc: Which kind of projection a Projection holds.

types.name: Fenrir::Projection
types.doc:
A camera's projection: exactly one of Perspective and Orthographic, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape.

Assign a kind to change it (`camera.projection = Orthographic{20.0f}`); read or edit it through the checked view (`camera.projection.As<Perspective>().verticalFov = 1.2f`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::Reflections
types.doc: A view's screen-space reflections (ADR-0056): what is on screen mirrored in smooth surfaces, from the previous frame's colour, over the sky's reflection. Each pixel's mirror ray is traced through a hierarchical-Z pyramid of the view's depth, from its vertex normal, and every material lighting through `Fenrir/Lighting.glsl` takes the colour it hit by how sure the hit is and how smooth the material is. They catch only what is on screen: what is off it, or hidden, falls back to the sky's reflection. They show last frame's colour, so a moving object's reflection trails it by a frame.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether the view has them: off by default, and off costs nothing. On, the view keeps about 44 MB at 1920 x 1080 across frames, and 17 MB more within each frame.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: How much of a sure reflection replaces the sky's: 1 by default, 0 turns them off.

fields.name: maxDistance
fields.doc: How far a mirror ray is traced, in world units: 50 by default. Reflections fade out towards it.

fields.name: thickness
fields.doc: How far behind a surface, in view depth (world units), a ray may pass and still hit it: 0.5 by default. Thicker catches thin things seen edge on; thinner stops rays catching on what they pass behind.

fields.name: roughnessCutoff
fields.doc: The roughness at and above which a surface reflects only the sky: 0.6 by default, fading in from 0.1 below it, as a blurred screen is a worse reflection than the sky's own.

types.name: Fenrir::ImageTarget
types.doc: A camera drawing into an image (ADR-0026): an RGBA8 sRGB ImageData with a size and no pixels, made with the asset store's Add and resized with Replace. Materials sample it like any image.

types.name: Fenrir::RenderTargetType
types.doc: Which kind of render target a RenderTarget holds.

types.name: Fenrir::WindowId
types.doc: Which window an input came from. A plain number chosen by whoever feeds the input (FenrirWindow, which keys its windows by it, or a test); FenrirInput only compares it.

types.name: Fenrir::WindowTarget
types.doc: A camera drawing into a window. The foundation renderer draws to the main window only.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: The main window by default (Window::MainWindow()). A camera naming another window is not drawn.

types.name: Fenrir::RenderTarget
types.doc: Where a camera's view goes: exactly one of WindowTarget and ImageTarget, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape. Assign a kind to change it (`camera.target = ImageTarget{image}`); read it through the checked view (`camera.target.As<ImageTarget>().image`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::Tonemapper
types.doc: How a view's Output pass maps its linear HDR colour, after the exposure, into the [0, 1] its render target stores, which the target then encodes as sRGB (ADR-0049).

values.name: None
values.doc: Each channel clamped to [0, 1]: what is over 1 is lost. For tests and exact colours.

values.name: AgX
values.doc: AgX, as Blender and Filament fit it: bright colours desaturate towards white as they would on film, and mid grey shows a little brighter than with None. The default.

values.name: PbrNeutral
values.doc: Khronos PBR Neutral: colours up to about 0.76 shown as they are (less a small offset in the darks), only the highlights compressed, so a material's base colour reads true.

values.name: Aces
values.doc: ACES, through Stephen Hill's fit of its reference rendering and sRGB output: contrasty, saturated.

types.name: Fenrir::Viewport
types.doc: The rectangle of its render target a view draws into, as fractions of the target's width and height from its top-left corner. The whole target by default.

types.name: Fenrir::Vignette
types.doc: A view's vignette (ADR-0059): the exposed colour darkened towards the corners, as a lens's falloff darkens them, before the grade and the tonemap, so the tonemapper sees it. Off by default, and off costs nothing.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: How much of the light the corners lose, from 0 to 1: 0 by default, off; 1 makes them black.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: Where the darkening starts, as a distance from the view's centre: 0 at the centre, 1 at the corners. 0.5 by default.

fields.name: smoothness
fields.doc: How far past the radius, in the same distance, the darkening takes to reach its intensity: 0.5 by default. 0 is a hard edge.

fields.name: roundness
fields.doc: The darkening's shape, from 0 to 1: 1 by default, a circle whatever the view's aspect; 0 an ellipse in the view's own proportions, reaching as far into the long sides as into the short ones.

types.name: Fenrir::Camera
types.doc:
Makes a view of the active scene from its entity, looking along the entity's local -Z with +Y up (ADR-0026). Plain data. Every enabled camera in the active scene draws one view a frame, into its viewport of its render target. Views into one target draw by `order`, lowest first, and ties by entity id, logged once. Each view has its own scene targets, and writes only its viewport.

Not drawn, logged once: a camera targeting a window other than the main window, a viewport under one pixel, or a target image that is stale, empty or not a render target. A minimised window draws nothing. A window no camera draws into is cleared to black, logged once.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: False draws no view.

fields.name: order
fields.doc: Views into one target draw lowest order first, so a higher order draws over a lower one.

fields.name: drawDebug
fields.doc: Whether the view draws the scene's debug shapes and world text (ADR-0025). Screen text and messages belong to the window, not the view, and draw either way.

fields.name: exposure
fields.doc: The view's exposure in EV stops: its Output pass multiplies the linear colour by 2^exposure before the tonemapper, so each +1 doubles it. 0 by default.

fields.name: tonemapper
fields.doc: How the view's Output pass maps its HDR colour into what its target stores (ADR-0049).

fields.name: bloom
fields.doc: How the view's bright pixels bleed into their surroundings before the tonemap.

fields.name: anamorphicStreaks
fields.doc: How the view's bright pixels draw out into horizontal lines before the tonemap, after bloom.

fields.name: lensFlare
fields.doc: The view's ghosts, halo and lens dirt before the tonemap, after the streaks.

fields.name: colourGrading
fields.doc: The look of the view: its white balance, contrast, tints and saturation, before the tonemap.

fields.name: chromaticAberration
fields.doc: How the view's colours fringe towards its corners, as it reads the scene.

fields.name: vignette
fields.doc: How the view darkens towards its corners, before the grade.

fields.name: filmGrain
fields.doc: The view's film grain, after its tonemap.

fields.name: ambientOcclusion
fields.doc: How nearby geometry darkens the sky's light in the view.

fields.name: reflections
fields.doc: How smooth surfaces in the view mirror what is on screen.

fields.name: debugView
fields.doc: What the view shows: its lit colour, or one of its inputs.

types.name: Fenrir::ColourSky
types.doc: A sky of one colour, which lights every surface with that colour from every side (ADR-0047).

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. A dark grey by default, the sky of a scene with none.

types.name: Fenrir::CubemapSky
types.doc: A sky drawn from a cubemap image (ImageShape::Cubemap, such as one loaded from a `.cubemap` file), sampled by the direction each pixel looks along, so it stays put as the camera moves and turns with it.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on what the sky draws.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: How far the sky is turned about world +Y, in radians, counter-clockwise seen from above: a quarter turn brings what was ahead (-Z) round to the left (-X).

types.name: Fenrir::DirectionalLight
types.doc:
The light shining along its entity's world -Z (ADR-0024). The renderer uses the first one in the active scene and warns once if there are more.

It casts shadows unless `castShadows` is off (ADR-0050): each camera gets cascaded shadow maps out to `shadowDistance`, up to RendererConfig::shadowCascades of them, split by RendererConfig::shadowSplitLambda, blended across their boundaries and fading out at the last. Each cascade is snapped to whole texels of its map, so its shadows hold still as the camera moves and turns. Edges are filtered by 16 rotated taps of hardware depth comparison. The biases trade shadow acne (speckled self-shadowing on lit faces) against peter-panning (shadows coming loose from their casters): raise them for acne, lower them for gaps.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. White by default (Colour::White).

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on the colour.

fields.name: castShadows
fields.doc: Whether it casts shadows: on by default.

fields.name: shadowDistance
fields.doc: How far from each camera, along its view, its shadows reach, in world units: 100 by default. Past it, everything is lit. The nearer it is, the sharper the shadows within it.

fields.name: shadowNormalBias
fields.doc: How far a lit point moves out along its normal before its shadow is looked up, in shadow-map texels (each cascade's own size): 1 by default.

fields.name: shadowSlopeBias
fields.doc: How far it moves towards the light, in texels per unit of slope (the tangent of the angle between its normal and the light, held between 0.1 and 8): 2 by default.

types.name: Fenrir::Entity
types.doc: Entity class that is used to interact with the entity list. This forms the basis of the ECS

types.name: Fenrir::InstancedMeshRenderer
types.doc:
Draws one mesh with one material many times, once per transform of an instance list, with no entity per copy (ADR-0051). Each copy is drawn at the entity's world matrix times its own transform, its colour multiplying the material's base colour in builtin:lit and builtin:unlit. The renderer uploads the list when it is new or its revision has moved on, so a list that never changes uploads once, however far the entity moves.

One draw a pass, whatever the count: never merged with other items. Its world bounds are the box around every copy's mesh box (ADR-0057; Renderer::GetWorldBounds), by which a camera it is wholly outside of leaves the whole list out; an opaque or masked list's copies are then culled one by one in the camera's cull pass, and a transparent list is sorted whole by the entity's world position. An empty or stale mesh or list is skipped (a stale one logged once per handle), as is a mesh with skin data; an empty or stale material draws with the fallback material, as a MeshRenderer's does.

fields.name: castShadows
fields.doc: Whether the copies are drawn into shadow maps, as a MeshRenderer's castShadows says.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: False hides every copy; the entity's children are drawn as their own renderers say.

types.name: Fenrir::Math::Ray
types.doc: Represents a ray in 3D space defined by an origin point and a direction vector.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: The origin point of the ray.

fields.name: dir
fields.doc: The direction vector of the ray, should be normalized to represent a direction.

types.name: Fenrir::MeshRenderer
types.doc:
Draws one mesh with one material at its entity's world transform (ADR-0023): one MeshRenderer, one draw. Plain data, read by the renderer from the active scene every Render; a mesh with several materials is several child entities, each with its own MeshRenderer.

An empty or stale mesh is skipped (a stale one logged once per handle). An empty or stale material draws with the fallback material, flat magenta and unlit, logged once per handle. An entity with no Transform draws at the origin.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: False hides this entity only; its children are drawn as their own MeshRenderers say.

fields.name: castShadows
fields.doc: Whether it is drawn into shadow maps: the sun's cascades and the shadowed spot and point lights' (ADR-0050). Only an `Opaque` or `Masked` material casts, a Masked one cut out by its alpha cutoff; `AlphaBlend` and `Additive` ones never do.

types.name: Fenrir::PanoramaSky
types.doc: A sky drawn from a panorama (ADR-0047): a flat image twice as wide as it is high wrapping the whole sphere, usually a linear HDR one such as an `.hdr` file. Its centre is ahead (-Z), its right half turns towards +X and its top row is straight up (+Y). The renderer turns it into a cube texture on the GPU once per image revision, then draws it as a CubemapSky.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on what the sky draws.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: How far the sky is turned about world +Y, in radians, as CubemapSky::rotation.

types.name: Fenrir::PointLight
types.doc:
A light shining from its entity's world position in every direction (ADR-0048), any number per scene. Its light falls with the square of the distance, windowed smoothly to zero at `range`: a white light of intensity 1 one unit straight above a white rough face lights it about as a DirectionalLight of intensity 1 does, when its range is well past one unit. A light that can light nothing (range or intensity 0, or black) is skipped.

With `castShadows` on it casts shadows (ADR-0050) while it is within RendererConfig::pointShadowBudget: each frame the shadowed point lights nearest to any camera keep them, each drawn into a cube of one shared cube array, as far as its range, and the rest light unshadowed, warned about once. Edges are filtered and biased as the DirectionalLight's are. A mesh round the light's position, such as a glowing bulb, shadows everything: turn that mesh's castShadows off.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. White by default (Colour::White).

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on the colour.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: The distance, in world units, at which the light has fallen to zero; nothing past it is lit.

fields.name: castShadows
fields.doc: Whether the light casts shadows: off by default. Only RendererConfig::pointShadowBudget of them do in a frame, the nearest to the cameras.

fields.name: shadowNormalBias
fields.doc: How far a lit point moves out along its normal before its shadow is looked up, in shadow-map texels (whose size grows with the distance from the light): 1 by default.

fields.name: shadowSlopeBias
fields.doc: How far it moves towards the light, in texels per unit of slope (the tangent of the angle between its normal and the light, held between 0.1 and 8): 2 by default.

types.name: Fenrir::RectLight
types.doc: A glowing rectangle centred on its entity, `width` along its world +X and `height` along its world +Y, shining from its face towards its world -Z (and from its back too when `twoSided`), any number per scene (ADR-0048). Its highlights take its shape, blurring with the surface's roughness: it is shaded with linearly transformed cosines, and casts no shadows. Its intensity is its radiance: a white rect light of intensity 1 filling the view of a white rough face lights it about 1, and one subtending less lights it less, as the sky does. Its light is windowed smoothly to zero at `range` from the rectangle. The rectangle itself is not drawn: give it an emissive mesh to see it. A light that can light nothing (range, intensity, width or height 0, or black) is skipped.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. White by default (Colour::White).

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on the colour.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Its size along its entity's world +X, in world units; the entity's scale does not stretch it.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Its size along its entity's world +Y, in world units.

fields.name: twoSided
fields.doc: Whether it shines from its back face as well as its front.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: The distance from the rectangle, in world units, at which its light has fallen to zero.

fields.name: visibleSurface
fields.doc: Whether the scene draws the light's surface, an emissive mesh where it is: true by default. Then, in a camera with reflections, its specular yields to the reflection of that surface where it is on screen, so it is not reflected twice. Set it false for a light with nothing drawn, which keeps its specular everywhere.

types.name: Fenrir::RendererStats
types.doc: What the renderer did in its last drawn frame (ADR-0023), except `instancesDrawn` and `drawnByLod`, read back from the most recent frame that has left flight (ADR-0057).

fields.name: draws
fields.doc: Draws of MeshRenderers in each view's Opaque and Transparent passes: one per run of matching opaque or masked items merged into an instanced draw (ADR-0051), and one per transparent item.

fields.name: instances
fields.doc: MeshRenderers drawn, one per item per view, however many draws they took, and the copies of each InstancedMeshRenderer's instance list, one per copy per view.

fields.name: instancesDrawn
fields.doc: MeshRenderers and instance list copies the GPU drew after each camera's cull pass (ADR-0057), summed over cameras, read back from the most recent frame that has left flight: usually two frames behind `instances`, the candidates this frame submitted. 0 until a frame has been read back.

fields.name: drawnByLod
fields.doc: `instancesDrawn` by the level of detail each was drawn at (ADR-0057): entry `i` the MeshRenderers and copies drawn at level `i` of their mesh (level 0 its full detail), the last entry those drawn at that level or any coarser, so the entries sum to `instancesDrawn`.

fields.name: passes
fields.doc: Render passes run.

fields.name: uploads
fields.doc: Assets uploaded to the GPU by the prepare step: a mesh, a material's parameter block, or an instance list.

fields.name: paletteBytesUploaded
fields.doc: Bytes copied into the frame's palette buffer: every skeleton palette the frame's draws read.

fields.name: distinctPalettesWritten
fields.doc: Skeleton palettes written, one per skeleton and pose however many meshes and views draw it (ADR-0035).

fields.name: skinnedDraws
fields.doc: Skinned MeshRenderers drawn, one per item per view; part of `instances`.

fields.name: shadowDraws
fields.doc: Draws into the sun's shadow cascades and the spot lights' shadow tiles (ADR-0050): one per run of matching casting items, merged as in `draws`, per cascade of each view, per shadowed spot light, and per shadowed point light (six times over for items whose shader draws its six faces one at a time).

types.name: Fenrir::SkinnedMesh
types.doc:
Skins the MeshRenderer beside it from a skeleton's pose (ADR-0035): plain data naming the skeleton entity, the entity carrying FenrirSkeleton's `SkeletonPose`. The mesh is drawn on the GPU from that skeleton's palette.

**A skinned item is drawn with the skeleton entity's world matrix. The mesh entity's own Transform and its ancestors are never applied**, unlike an ordinary MeshRenderer's: the mesh's vertices are already in the skeleton's bind space. `visible` and the material stay on the mesh entity's MeshRenderer. SpawnModel makes each skinned mesh entity a child of its skeleton entity at the identity, so the hierarchy reads naturally.

A mesh with skin data and no SkinnedMesh is not drawn; nor is one whose skeleton entity is dead, has no `SkeletonPose` or is not `Ready`, whose skeleton it was not baked for (more bones than the skeleton has, or a different bind signature), or when no skinning source is registered (FenrirSkeleton is not installed). A user shader without the `SKINNED` key draws it with the fallback material. Each is logged once as a warning. A SkinnedMesh on a mesh with no skin data is ignored, and the mesh draws rigidly (logged once).

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity whose pose skins the mesh.

types.name: Fenrir::SkyType
types.doc: Which kind of sky a Sky holds.

types.name: Fenrir::Sky
types.doc:
What a scene shows where nothing was drawn, and the light every surface takes from all round it, a scene resource (ADR-0026, ADR-0047): exactly one of ColourSky, CubemapSky and PanoramaSky, by value, as FenrirPhysics' CollisionShape holds a shape. A scene without one has the default ColourSky, a dark grey. Each camera whose background is SceneBackground draws it; a ColourBackground replaces only what that camera's view draws behind the scene, and every view is lit by the scene's Sky.

The renderer filters a cubemap or panorama sky on the GPU into image-based lighting, once per image revision: its intensity scales the light, and its rotation turns it, without filtering again. A SkyLight lights the scene in its place, leaving it drawn.

A cubemap that is empty, stale or not a cubemap with pixels, or a panorama that is empty, stale, or not a flat image with pixels twice as wide as high, draws the default ColourSky instead, logged once. Assign a kind to change it (`sky = PanoramaSky{image}`); read it through the checked view. Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::SkyLight
types.doc:
What lights the scene from all round, when it is not the Sky drawn behind it, a scene resource (ADR-0047): a sky of any kind, used only for its light. A scene without one is lit by its Sky. A skybox chosen for how it looks can light the scene with a neutral ColourSky or a softer panorama instead of its own colours, as a camera's ColourBackground changes what is drawn and not the light. One sky lights the scene either way, so nothing is lit twice.

Its sky is read as the Sky is: a cubemap or panorama that cannot be drawn lights with the default ColourSky, logged once, and its intensity and rotation scale and turn the light without filtering it again.

fields.name: sky
fields.doc: The sky the scene is lit by: the default ColourSky, a dark grey, unless set.

types.name: Fenrir::SpotLight
types.doc:
A light shining from its entity's world position along its world -Z in a cone (ADR-0048), any number per scene. It falls off with distance as a PointLight does, and across its cone smoothly from full inside `innerAngle` to none outside `outerAngle`, both measured from its axis. A light that can light nothing is skipped.

With `castShadows` on it casts shadows (ADR-0050) while it is within RendererConfig::spotShadowBudget: each frame the shadowed spot lights nearest to any camera keep them, each drawn into a tile of one shared atlas through a perspective along its cone (held to 80 degrees off its axis), and the rest light unshadowed, warned about once. Edges are filtered and biased as the DirectionalLight's are. A mesh round the light's position, such as a glowing bulb, shadows all of its cone: turn that mesh's castShadows off.

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: Linear. White by default (Colour::White).

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: A plain multiplier on the colour.

fields.name: range
fields.doc: The distance, in world units, at which the light has fallen to zero; nothing past it is lit.

fields.name: innerAngle
fields.doc: The angle off its axis, in radians, inside which the cone is fully lit: 0 by default, as glTF's.

fields.name: outerAngle
fields.doc: The angle off its axis, in radians, outside which nothing is lit: 45 degrees by default, as glTF's.

fields.name: castShadows
fields.doc: Whether the light casts shadows: off by default. Only RendererConfig::spotShadowBudget of them do in a frame, the nearest to the cameras.

fields.name: shadowNormalBias
fields.doc: How far a lit point moves out along its normal before its shadow is looked up, in shadow-map texels (whose size grows with the distance from the light): 1 by default.

fields.name: shadowSlopeBias
fields.doc: How far it moves towards the light, in texels per unit of slope (the tangent of the angle between its normal and the light, held between 0.1 and 8): 2 by default.
